## Goal

Lock the distinction between volume capacity and file-detail scope, the minimum human and agent evidence bundle, bounded privacy behavior, and the lifecycle of a capped multi-slice scan generation.

## Deliverables

- Actionable export contract
- Scope and coverage vocabulary
- Capped scan-generation state machine
- Contract fixtures and tests

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-C250-01` — The contract names volume-capacity scope, configured file-detail roots, exclusions, completed versus partial scan generations, open gaps, retained precision, and state-as-of times separately so none can imply broader coverage.
- `AC-C250-02` — A human-triggered evidence bundle has one consistent database view and includes an actionable brief plus machine-readable summary, current state, changes or rollups, provenance, agent sessions, coverage, lifecycle, snapshots, manifest, and integrity data without file contents or environment values.
- `AC-C250-03` — The brief leads with monitored scope, coverage confidence, largest current consumers, recent growth or its absence, cleanup-review leads, evidence age, limitations, and an explicit inspection order; exact records remain bounded by retained database policy and may be compressed.
- `AC-C250-04` — A capped scan slice cannot reconcile absence or deletion; durable generation progress survives restart, and only completion of every included root can atomically advance current state and change history for that generation.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-C250-01` (evidence-usefulness-contract-test) — Schema fixtures distinguish scope and coverage, reject missing bundle roles and false no-limitations claims, and model multi-slice completion, restart, scope change, and abandoned generation behavior.
